title: From atomic events to material degradation across metre and year scales
abstract: arXiv:2611.28559v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Material degradation emerges from microscopic events whose consequences accumulate over years, yet mechanism-resolved simulations remain confined below engineering timescales. The challenge is not just the sheer number of events: atomistic evolution is dominated by recurrent local motion, with only a tiny fraction driving lasting structural change. This distinction is not encoded in an instantaneous atomic configuration. Locally indistinguishable states can exhibit different event competition, escape times, and long-horizon outcomes, revealing missing kinetic context as a critical information bottleneck. This context spans space and time: the future consequence of a local transition depends on its surrounding defect environment and the kinetic history leading to its current state. translated_title: 从原子事件到米级与年际尺度的材料退化
translated_abstract: 材料退化源于微观事件，其后果经过多年累积，然而机理分辨的模拟仍局限于工程时间尺度以下。挑战不仅在于事件数量庞大：原子尺度的演化由反复出现的局部运动主导，其中仅有一小部分驱动持久的结构变化。这一区别并未编码在瞬时的原子构型之中。局部上不可区分的状态可能表现出不同的事件竞争、逃逸时间和长期演化结果，这揭示了缺失的动力学背景是一个关键的信息瓶颈。这种背景跨越空间和时间：一个局部转变的未来后果取决于其周围的缺陷环境以及导致其达到当前状态的动力学历史。为解决这一问题，AtomWorld从多尺度结构观测和轨迹历史中重建预测性动力学状态，区分瞬态涨落（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出AtomWorld框架，通过融合多尺度结构观测与轨迹历史来重建预测性动力学状态，突破了瞬时原子构型无法编码关键动力学背景的信息瓶颈，从而实现从原子事件到米级、年际尺度的材料退化模拟与预测。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes AtomWorld, a framework that reconstructs predictive kinetic states from multiscale structural observations and trajectory history, overcoming the information bottleneck of instantaneous atomic configurations to enable material degradation simulation from atomic events up to metre and year scales.
